question: What is another name for healthcare-associated infections?
explanation: Healthcare-associated infections are commonly referred to as nosocomial infections, acquired during the process of receiving medical care. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses play the most critical role in infection control?

options.A: They diagnose the specific type of microbial pathogen in the laboratory.
options.B: They purchase all the hospital cleaning chemicals and supplies.
options.C: They maintain continuous patient contact and execute daily safety protocols.
options.D: They write the national health policies regarding hospital sanitation.

explanation: Nurses are at the bedside constantly, placing them in the best position to monitor and enforce infection prevention practices. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which bloodborne viruses are most commonly transmitted by unsafe injections?

options.A: Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV

explanation: Unsafe parenteral practices primarily spread blood-borne pathogens such as Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and human immunodeficiency virus. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h2)

question: What defines a safe injection?

options.A: It is given only through the veins using plastic syringes.
options.B: It causes no pain at the exact spot where the needle enters.
options.C: It cures the patient completely within one day.
options.D: It harms no one, puts the worker at no avoidable risk, and leaves safe waste.

explanation: A safe injection balances patient safety, worker protection, and proper community waste management. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is the single most effective intervention to prevent cross-contamination?
explanation: Proper hand cleansing removes transient flora and remains the primary method to halt the spread of nosocomial pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h3)

question: When can you use an alcohol-based hand rub instead of soap and water?

options.A: When hands are not visibly dirty or soiled with body fluids
options.B: After helping a patient with severe diarrhea
options.C: Before leaving the hospital at the end of a shift
options.D: When caring for a patient with active tuberculosis

explanation: Alcohol rubs work well for routine hand cleaning as long as there is no visible dirt or organic matter on the hands. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why must an alcohol-swabbed vial top dry before you insert the needle?

options.A: To keep the rubber top from becoming too soft to pierce
options.B: To stop the medicine from changing color inside the glass
options.C: To give the alcohol enough time to kill germs effectively
options.D: To cool down the vial after rubbing it

explanation: Chemical disinfectants need adequate contact time through air drying to properly kill germs on surfaces. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which action is a break in aseptic technique when preparing an injection?

options.A: Waiting for the alcohol-swabbed vial top to dry completely
options.B: Checking the medication label three times against the chart
options.C: Opening the sterile syringe package right before use
options.D: Touching the inner sterile plunger shaft while drawing up medication

explanation: The inner plunger and needle must stay sterile; touching them transfers skin germs directly into the medication. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h4)

question: How full should a sharps box be before it is sealed and replaced?
explanation: Sealing sharps boxes at three-quarters capacity prevents needles from sticking out and causing accidental injuries during disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why should you avoid recapping needles with two hands?

options.A: It wastes too much time during busy medication rounds.
options.B: It violates hospital rules on plastic recycling.
options.C: It makes the needle blunt and unusable.
options.D: It greatly increases the chance of an accidental needle-stick injury.

explanation: Holding the cap with one hand while guiding the needle makes it easy to miss the cap and stab yourself. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you experience an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Squeeze the wound hard to force out the blood
options.B: Cover the injury tightly with a plaster
options.C: Wash the site with soap and running water
options.D: Apply strong antiseptic bleach to the puncture wound

explanation: Immediate washing removes surface germs without damaging the tissue further or helping viruses enter. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why is time so important when starting treatment after an HIV needle-stick injury?

options.A: Antiviral drugs work best when started quickly before the virus multiplies.
options.B: Hospital insurance policies expire within twenty-four hours.
options.C: Delayed treatment causes permanent nerve damage in your finger.
options.D: Lab tests for the patient take a full day to process.

explanation: Starting treatment early helps stop the virus before it can set up a permanent infection in the body. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h6)

question: What common misunderstanding do many patients have about injections compared to tablets?

options.A: Injections are less expensive than tablets
options.B: Tablets are only useful for long-term illnesses
options.C: Oral medications have more toxic side effects
options.D: Injections always work faster than oral medications

explanation: Patients often request injections because they believe they provide much faster and better healing than pills. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h7)

question: How does educating patients about injection safety help the wider community?

options.A: It stops patients from visiting local medicine vendors.
options.B: It means nurses no longer have to check sharps boxes.
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of buying intravenous fluids for the ward.
options.D: It encourages patients to question unsafe practices and lowers the demand for unnecessary injections.

explanation: Awareness helps patients ask for sterile equipment, which reduces the spread of infections across local healthcare settings. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h7)
